h1: Ocean View Resort - Koh Sichang — a small seaside resort on Koh Sichang where you wake up to the sea
intro: If you want to escape Bangkok and fall asleep to the sound of waves on an island that's just a 45-minute boat ride from Sriracha, Ocean View Resort - Koh Sichang is the little resort plenty of people talk about · It's a seaside stay in the Tha Thewawong area of Koh Sichang with around 16 rooms, many of which open onto a balcony with a full view of the sea and mountains · What guests agree on is the sea views, breakfast included in the rate, and the owner who looks after guests with real care · Prices start at around THB 1,500/night · Scored 7.5 from 60 reviews on Trip.com (location 7.8 · service 7.4) — a simple resort that sells island atmosphere rather than luxury

body.html: Overview and who this place suits — If you had to sum up Ocean View Resort - Koh Sichang in one sentence, this is a small, owner-run resort that clearly sells two things: seaside views by the island and the quiet, peaceful atmosphere of Koh Sichang · It isn't a luxury resort with a private beach, it isn't a big-chain hotel with an infinity pool and a spa, and it isn't a place that will pamper you with every amenity · It's a roughly 16-room 2-star resort that has been open since 2016, set on the seafront in the Tha Thewawong area, on an island that's only about a 45-minute boat ride from the Koh Loy pier in Sriracha · Real reviews on Trip.com, Booking.com and Expedia all point the same way: the people who suit this place are travellers who want quiet and sea views more than luxury — couples escaping the bustle of the city to fall asleep to the waves, small families coming over to Koh Sichang for a night, groups of friends who want to cycle around the island and come back to relax on the balcony, and workers looking for somewhere quiet to unwind over the weekend · On the flip side, if you expect a white-sand beach resort where you step out of your room straight into the water, with a pool, a gym, or five-star service, this place may not be what you're after, and you should adjust your expectations or look at a stay over on the Pattaya side instead · But for anyone who understands they're paying a few thousand baht for "a seaside room on the island where you open the balcony and there's the view," Ocean View Resort does that job well enough, and that's why it still earns an overall 7.5 from 60 reviews — which is solid for a small stay at this price on an island where there aren't many options.

Location and getting there — This is something to understand clearly before you book, because getting to Koh Sichang isn't like driving to Bangsaen or Pattaya · Koh Sichang is an island that forms one district of Chonburi, sitting off the coast of Sriracha district, and the main way to get there is to take the ferry from the Koh Loy pier in Sriracha, which costs around 50–60 baht per person and takes about 45 minutes; ferries run roughly every hour from morning to evening (around 7:00 AM–6:00 PM heading to the island), or if you're in a hurry there's a speedboat that takes around 15–20 min at a higher price · From Bangkok, it's about an hour and a half to two hours' drive to Sriracha, where you park on the Sriracha side before getting on the boat, because you don't need to bring a private car onto the island · Once you reach the island, Ocean View Resort is in the Tha Thewawong area, not far from the pier, and many reviews say the resort helps arrange a pickup or recommends a skylab (the island's shared songthaew) · Getting around the island, people usually charter a skylab for around 300–700 baht depending on how many stops you make, or rent a bicycle or motorbike · One thing about the location that foreign reviews mention is that the resort sits more toward the quiet side, not in the middle of the shopping area, which is a plus for anyone after peace and quiet, but those who want to walk out to several restaurants within walking distance may feel they need a vehicle · In short, this kind of location suits people who genuinely come to relax on the island and are ready to plan their travel around the boat and the island's local transport, more than people used to the convenience of driving right up to the hotel door.

"It's only a forty-five-minute boat ride from Sriracha, and the moment I opened the room door to a balcony looking over the sea, all the tiredness disappeared. So quiet, perfect for coming to rest and escape the city. The owner is kind, helped recommend places to visit and even called a car for us."

Rooms and decor — Ocean View Resort has around 16 rooms across several levels, from the Standard Room (Double bed), the simple entry-level room, to the Superior Room (Queen bed) and Deluxe Room (Queen bed), which usually come with a balcony and a better view · The room's selling point is exactly what the resort's name promises — many rooms open onto a balcony with a full view of the sea and the mountains of Koh Sichang, and plenty of reviews agree the balcony is fairly wide, comfortable for sipping morning coffee or watching the sunset · Rooms have air conditioning, a fridge, free drinking water, a private bathroom, and the basics, and some have a sofa or an extra sofa bed · The decor is the style of a small, simple resort in easy-on-the-eye tones, focused on being practical and giving a homely, friendly feel rather than bold design · What guests praise most often is the comfortable bed, lovely view, and quiet atmosphere, well suited to resting · But to be straight with you, you have to set your expectations to a 2-star level and a building that has been open since 2016 · Some reviews note room condition and cleanliness that isn't consistent across every room, sometimes a broken bathroom door, some rooms with no hot water or hot water that's inconsistent, and a few people feel the room they actually get doesn't quite match the photos on the booking site · The advice is to specify from the moment you book that you want a room with a sea-view balcony, and ideally contact the resort directly to ask about the room condition and hot water before you travel, to reduce the chance of disappointment.

Facilities and the common areas — As a small resort, the common areas of Ocean View Resort focus on being right-sized and on the seaside atmosphere rather than grandeur · The highlight is the seaside terrace and garden where you can sit, catch the breeze and take in the view, along with a barbecue corner for anyone who wants to grill by the sea in the evening · The resort offers bicycle rental, a popular way to tour Koh Sichang at a relaxed pace, and there's free parking for those riding a motorbike or with a vehicle on the island · Free Wi-Fi is available, and most reviews say it works in the common areas and in the rooms, even if the signal across the island overall may not be as strong as in the city · To be honest, there's no swimming pool, no gym, and no spa here, in the style of a small island resort, so if these matter to your trip, this place may not be the answer · But what makes up for it is the island itself — just a short way out of the resort you'll find seaside spots and a beach for swimming · Another thing many reviews mention positively is that the resort is pet-friendly and has cats to play with, giving it a warm, friendly, home-like feel rather than a hotel one.

Food and places to eat nearby — One thing Ocean View Resort does well and gets consistent praise for is the breakfast included in the room rate · Many reviews say breakfast is freshly made and tastes good, and some specifically praise getting to eat breakfast with a sea view in a quiet setting, which was a memorable part of the trip · The resort also has an on-site restaurant open for both lunch and dinner plus room service, so you don't have to go far if you can't be bothered to travel · Because the resort sits in a fairly quiet area, not in the middle of the market, having its own kitchen is a real plus for dinner · For anyone who wants to head out and try Koh Sichang's good food, there are seafood restaurants, cafes, and local eats to choose from around the pier and the market area, which you can reach by skylab or bicycle · Local specialities like fresh seafood and local fish dishes are what many people specifically come to the island to eat · The bottom line on food is that Ocean View Resort stands out for its breakfast and the convenience of having a restaurant on site, while for other meals a trip on the island gives you the chance to head out and try local spots — which is part of the charm of staying on an island anyway.

Service — Even as a small resort, service is actually the point that comes up most positively in the real reviews · The standout is that it's an owner-run resort, with many reviews naming the owner (Khun Santi) as kind, friendly, and helpful beyond expectations — whether recommending places to visit, calling a car, or sorting out the boat · The service feel leans warm and home-like rather than hotel-like, and people who like that friendliness are especially impressed by it · To be straight, as a small stay with limited staff, some service is the "ask and you'll get it" kind and may not be as systematic as a big hotel — for example, responses to bookings or handling certain things can take time · But overall the goodwill and care of the owner and the team are what guests remember positively, and a big reason people are willing to overlook the building's small limitations.

Voices from real reviews (both praise and criticism) — Pulling together reviews from Trip.com, Booking.com, Expedia and other booking sites, the picture is fairly consistent · On the praise side: what comes up most is the beautiful sea and mountain views, the wide balcony you can sit and enjoy the view from, the quiet, peaceful atmosphere good for resting, the tasty breakfast included in the rate, the comfortable bed, and — earning special praise — the friendly, helpful owner and staff · Many people sum it up as a stay that gives a quiet island atmosphere at an affordable price · On the watch-out side: the most-mentioned issue is room condition and cleanliness that isn't consistent, with some reviews finding a broken bathroom door or details that need fixing · Next is the hot water, which some rooms don't have or which is inconsistent, the actual room sometimes not matching the photos on the booking site, the location being fairly far from the island's main shopping area so you need a vehicle, and the facility limitations that come with a small resort · What's interesting is that most of these criticisms are things you'd find at a small island resort at this price point, and people who set their expectations right tend to score it higher than those expecting luxury, which keeps the overall score at a solid 7.5.

"Great view, you can relax on the balcony all day, tasty breakfast, lovely owner · The only downside is that the hot water in the bathroom of our room wasn't very strong; next time I'll call to check before booking, but overall it's worth it for the price and the island atmosphere."

Price comparison and value — The starting price at Ocean View Resort - Koh Sichang is around THB 1,500/night for the entry-level room on weekdays, rising to around THB 2,000–THB 2,500+ for a Superior or Deluxe room with a sea-view balcony, especially on weekends, long holidays, and festivals when people flock to Koh Sichang (the average rate shown on booking sites is around 40–74 dollars) · Compared with other stays on Koh Sichang, most of which are similar small resorts and guesthouses, Ocean View Resort positions itself in the budget group while still managing to offer a sea-view room with a balcony and breakfast included, which is what makes it good value within that group · If the goal of your trip is to "wake up to the sea on the island on a few-thousand-baht budget," this place does exactly that at an easily accessible price · Just remember that sea-view rooms and holiday dates are limited and fill up fast, because island stays have far fewer rooms than the mainland, so book ahead and ask about the room condition before you decide, so you get a room that genuinely matches what you want.

Things to know before booking — There are several things that help make a stay on the island smoother · One, plan the boat well: the ferry from the Koh Loy pier in Sriracha has limited departures (about every hour, around 7:00 AM–6:00 PM), so check the time of the last boat and sort out parking on the Sriracha side, since you don't need to bring a car onto the island · Two, specify a sea-view balcony room when you book, because it's the biggest highlight and makes a big difference to the atmosphere · Three, if you're worried about the hot water or room condition, try contacting the resort directly to ask before you travel, and keep in mind it's a small 2-star stay, not a luxury hotel · Four, prepare a plan for touring the island by skylab (chartered for around 300–700 baht) or by renting a bicycle or motorbike, and bring your personal items including any regular medication, because shops on the island are limited · Five, during long holidays and festivals, island stays fill up very fast, so book several weeks ahead and compare prices across platforms before deciding.

Verdict — From all the real reviews, Ocean View Resort - Koh Sichang is the best fit for anyone who wants to wake up to the sea on Koh Sichang in a quiet, peaceful setting, with a sea-view balcony, breakfast included, and an owner who looks after you, all on a few-thousand-baht budget · The strengths guests agree on are the sea and mountain views, the quiet, the breakfast, and the goodwill of the owner and the team · As for the watch-outs — room condition and cleanliness that isn't consistent, hot water in some rooms, a location that needs a vehicle, and facility limitations that come with a small resort — these are all things you can manage by choosing your room, asking ahead, and setting your expectations right · If you're after a white-sand beach resort with a pool, a spa, and five-star service, this isn't the answer, and you should consider options on the Pattaya side instead · But for a Koh Sichang trip where you want a quiet seaside stay at an affordable price, and you're ready to open up to the charm of a small island resort — Ocean View Resort delivers an atmosphere that lives up to its name, and that's why many people keep coming back to an island where stays like this aren't easy to find.

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Ocean View Resort - Koh Sichang

faq.q: Where is Ocean View Resort - Koh Sichang · how do you get there?
faq.a: The resort is set on the seafront in the Tha Thewawong area on Koh Sichang, Ko Si Chang District, Chonburi · Get there by taking the ferry across from the Koh Loy pier in Sriracha, fare around 50–60 baht per person, taking about 45 minutes (there's a speedboat at around 15–20 min) · From Bangkok, drive to Sriracha in about 1.5–2 hours, then park on the Sriracha side before getting on the boat; you don't need to bring a car onto the island

faq.q: What is the starting price at Ocean View Resort - Koh Sichang · what rooms are there?
faq.a: Prices start at around THB 1,500/night for a Standard room on weekdays · There are Superior and Deluxe rooms that usually come with a sea-view balcony, at around THB 1,900–THB 2,500 depending on the period · The average rate shown on booking sites is around 40–74 dollars · During holidays and festivals rooms fill up fast because island stays have few rooms, so book ahead

faq.q: Who does Ocean View Resort - Koh Sichang suit best?
faq.a: It suits couples, small families, and anyone who wants to escape the city to sleep by the sea on Koh Sichang in a quiet, peaceful setting on a few-thousand-baht budget · It stands out for the sea and mountain views, wide balcony, breakfast included, and the owner who looks after you · It isn't right for people who want a beach resort with a pool, a spa, or five-star service, for which the Pattaya side is a better fit

faq.q: Does Ocean View Resort - Koh Sichang have breakfast and a swimming pool?
faq.a: There's breakfast included in the room rate, freshly made and praised for its taste, plus an on-site restaurant open for lunch and dinner and room service · But there's no swimming pool, gym, or spa, in the style of a small island resort · There's a seaside terrace, a garden, a barbecue corner, bicycle rental, free parking, and free Wi-Fi

faq.q: What are the room condition and hot water like at Ocean View Resort?
faq.a: Most reviews praise the views and atmosphere, but some note that room condition and cleanliness aren't consistent across every room and that hot water in some rooms is inconsistent · We recommend contacting the resort directly to ask before you travel and specifying a sea-view balcony room in good condition, keeping in mind it's a small 2-star stay, not a luxury hotel

faq.q: Staying at Ocean View Resort - Koh Sichang, what is there to see nearby?
faq.a: Tour the island by skylab (chartered for around 300–700 baht) or by renting a bicycle · Highlights near the resort include Khao Khat viewpoint, the island's most beautiful sunset spot, Phra Chudadhuj Palace and Atsadang Bridge, Tham Pang Beach, the Chao Pho Khao Yai shrine, and Wat Tham Yai Prik · Most are within a 5–10 min drive
